items.message:
High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 07:15am to 11:15am on 23/10/2026. 
Locations most affected will be low lying land and roads near rivers or on the coast. Areas most at risk include Christchurch Harbour and tidal stretches of the Lower Stour and Avon. The detailed tidal forecast for those who use it is for a peak level at Christchurch of 1.25mAODN at 09:15 with NW force 6 winds. (mAODN is height above average sea level.) 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded.   
This message will be updated by 3:30PM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.

Forecast rising river levels overnight may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from the morning of Friday 23 October .
Locations most affected will be low lying land and roads near rivers. 
Areas most at risk are low-lying agricultural land and roads including Slash Lane at Sileby and the Mountsorrel to Sileby road. Rainfall is forecast this evening. River levels at Pillings Lock Gauge will begin rising from 21:00 on 22/10/26 therefore this pre emptive flood alert is being issued.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Avoid using low lying footpaths and any bridges near local watercourses.  
This message will be updated by 9:00AM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.

items.description: South Devon coast from Start Point to Dawlish Warren
items.eaAreaName: Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
items.message:
High tides, strong winds and large waves tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 2 hours either side of high tide on Friday morning 
Areas particularly at risk include Torbay, Teignmouth, Beesands, Torcross, Slapton and Dawlish.
  
The high tide at Exmouth on Friday is at 04:05 GMT, times of high water will vary along the coast.  Forecast total high tide level is 2.03mAOD, which is 0.81 metres above tide table level.  Strong force 7 north easterly winds and offshore wave heights of over 2.5m are forecast over the high tide.
Coastal conditions should ease for Friday evening's high tide. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.   
This message will be updated by 12:00PM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.

We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded.   
This message will be updated by 3:30PM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.

floodArea.riverOrSea: Ings Beck, Alverthorpe Beck, Balne Beck, Oakenshaw Beck

items.message:
Rising river levels overnight may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from the early hours of Friday 23 October .
Locations most affected will be Alverthorpe Beck, Balne Beck, Ings Beck and Oakenshaw Beck in Wakefield, low lying land and roads near rivers. Rain associated with Storm Austen overnight will see river levels rise from the early hours of Friday, peaking between 6:00AM and midday. Friday will be largely dry with levels falling through the day. Further rain is forecast on Saturday afternoon which may see levels rise again.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.  
This message will be updated by 9:00AM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.

Strong winds and large waves tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 03:20am to 11:00am on 23/10/2026 
Areas most at risk include Lyme Regis, Charmouth, Seatown, West Bay, Bothenhampton, Burton Freshwater, Burton Bradstock, Cogden Beach, Chesil Beach, West Fleet, East Fleet and particularly at Chiswell. Further flooding is possible at Chiswell throughout the morning due to Storm Austin bringing force 7 to 8 high winds and large waves. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Exposed coastal areas may be hazardous due to strong winds and large waves. Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded. 
This message will be updated by 2:30PM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.

Flooding is expected from 2 hours either side of high tide on Friday morning 
Areas particularly at risk include exposed coastal areas at Hallsands, Beesands, Torcross, Slapton, Blackpool Sands, Teignmouth Promenade and Dawlish.
 
The high tide at Teignmouth on Friday is at 03:55 GMT, times of high water will vary along the coast.  Forecast total high tide level is 2.11mAOD, which is 0.75 metres above tide table level.  Strong force 7 north easterly winds and offshore wave heights of over 2.5m are forecast over the high tide.

Coastal conditions should ease for Friday evening's high tide. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.   
This message will be updated by 12:00PM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.
